questionText: Which sentence uses a colon correctly?
option1: Bring these items: a pencil, a ruler and an eraser.
option2: Bring: these items a pencil, a ruler and an eraser.
option3: Bring these: items a pencil, a ruler and an eraser.
option4: Bring these items a pencil: a ruler and an eraser.
explanation: A colon can introduce a list after a complete clause.

questionText: Which sentence uses a semicolon correctly?
option1: The rain stopped; we went outside.
option2: The rain; stopped we went outside.
option3: The rain stopped we; went outside.
option4: The rain stopped; and we went outside.
explanation: A semicolon can join two closely related independent clauses.

questionText: Which sentence has the comma in the correct position?
option1: After the match we, went home.
option2: After the match, we went home.
option3: After, the match we went home.
option4: After the match we went, home.
explanation: An introductory phrase is followed by a comma.

questionText: Which sentence uses commas correctly for direct speech?
explanation: A comma separates the spoken words from the reporting clause in this construction.

questionText: Which sentence uses an apostrophe correctly?
explanation: The desk belongs to one teacher, so the singular possessive apostrophe is used.

questionText: Which sentence shows possession by more than one student?
option1: The students' books were on the table.
option2: The student's books were on the table.
option3: The students books' were on the table.
option4: The student' books were on the table.
explanation: The plural noun students takes an apostrophe after the s.

questionText: Which sentence uses brackets correctly?
option1: The lion (which was very old) slept in the sun.
option2: The lion which (was very old slept in the sun).
option3: The lion (which was very old slept) in the sun.
option4: The lion which was (very old) slept in the sun.
explanation: The bracketed words form a complete parenthetical phrase.

questionText: Which sentence uses a hyphen correctly?
option4: She wore a well known brand.
explanation: A compound adjective before a noun can use a hyphen: well-known brand.

questionText: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
explanation: A comma follows the introductory adverb However.

questionText: Which sentence is a complete sentence?
explanation: The third sentence contains a subject and a finite verb and expresses a complete thought.

questionText: Which sentence contains a subordinate clause?
option2: We stayed inside because it was raining.
explanation: Because it was raining is a subordinate clause introduced by because.

questionText: Which word introduces the subordinate clause in this sentence: 'Although it was late, we continued.'?
explanation: Although is the subordinating conjunction introducing the subordinate clause.

questionText: Which sentence contains two independent clauses joined correctly?
option1: I finished my homework, I watched television.
option2: I finished my homework; I watched television.
option3: I finished my homework because; I watched television.
option4: I finished; my homework I watched television.
explanation: A semicolon correctly joins the two independent clauses.

questionText: Which sentence is correctly punctuated?
option1: If you finish early, read quietly.
option2: If you finish early read, quietly.
option3: If, you finish early read quietly.
option4: If you finish, early read quietly.
explanation: The introductory if-clause is followed by a comma.

questionText: Which sentence uses a question mark correctly?
option3: She asked where did he go?
explanation: Where did she go? is a direct question and needs a question mark.

questionText: Which sentence uses an exclamation mark appropriately?
explanation: What a brilliant goal! is an exclamation expressing strong feeling.

questionText: Which sentence uses quotation marks correctly?
option1: The teacher said, "Please open your books."
option2: The teacher said, Please "open your books".
option3: The teacher "said, Please open your books."
option4: The teacher said, "Please open your books".
explanation: The full spoken sentence is enclosed in quotation marks, with punctuation inside.

questionText: Which sentence uses a comma to separate items in a list correctly?
option1: We bought apples bananas, pears and oranges.
option2: We bought apples, bananas, pears and oranges.
option3: We bought, apples bananas pears and oranges.
option4: We bought apples bananas pears, and oranges.
explanation: Commas separate the listed items.

questionText: Which sentence uses a comma correctly after a fronted adverbial?
option1: In the morning we walked to school.
option2: In the morning, we walked to school.
option3: In, the morning we walked to school.
option4: In the morning we, walked to school.
explanation: The introductory fronted adverbial In the morning is followed by a comma.

questionText: Which sentence avoids a comma splice?
option1: The sky darkened, the rain began.
option2: The sky darkened; the rain began.
option3: The sky; darkened the rain began.
option4: The sky darkened, and, the rain began.
explanation: A semicolon can correctly separate the two independent clauses.

questionText: Which sentence is in the present perfect tense?
explanation: Have finished is the present perfect construction.

questionText: Which sentence is in the past perfect tense?
option1: She had left before I arrived.
option3: She is leaving before I arrive.
option4: She will leave before I arrive.
explanation: Had left is the past perfect form.

questionText: Which sentence uses the future tense correctly?
option1: We will visit the museum tomorrow.
option4: We have visit the museum tomorrow.
explanation: Will visit expresses a future action.

questionText: Choose the correct verb: 'Neither of the answers ___ correct.'
explanation: Neither is treated as singular in this sentence, so is is correct.

questionText: Choose the correct verb: 'The list of names ___ on the desk.'
explanation: The subject is list, which is singular.

questionText: Choose the correct verb: 'The children ___ playing outside.'
explanation: Children is plural, so are is correct.

questionText: Which sentence uses the past continuous correctly?
option1: I was reading when the phone rang.
option2: I were reading when the phone rang.
option3: I am reading when the phone rang.
option4: I had read when the phone rang.
explanation: Was reading describes an ongoing action interrupted by the phone ringing.

questionText: Which sentence uses the present continuous correctly?
option1: They are studying for the test.
option2: They is studying for the test.
option4: They were study for the test.
explanation: The present continuous uses are plus the -ing form for they.

questionText: Which sentence uses the past simple correctly?
option1: We went to York last weekend.
option2: We have went to York last weekend.
option3: We go to York last weekend.
option4: We were go to York last weekend.
explanation: Went is the correct past simple form of go.

questionText: Which sentence uses an irregular past tense correctly?
option3: She buy a new book yesterday.
option4: She had buyed a new book.
explanation: Bought is the irregular past tense of buy.

questionText: Which sentence uses a modal verb correctly?
option2: You must to finish your work.
explanation: A modal verb is followed by the base form of the main verb.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'should' correctly?
explanation: Should is followed by the base verb revise.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'might' correctly?
explanation: Might is followed by the base verb rain.

questionText: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
option2: The meal was cooked by the chef.
option3: The chef is cooking the meal.
option4: The chef will cook the meal.
explanation: The meal receives the action in the passive construction was cooked.

questionText: Which sentence changes the active sentence 'The storm damaged the roof' into the passive voice?
option1: The roof was damaged by the storm.
option3: The storm was damaged by the roof.
option4: The roof has damage the storm.
explanation: The object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses 'has'?
explanation: She takes has, followed by the past participle finished.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses 'have'?
explanation: They takes have, followed by the past participle finished.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses 'did' in a question?
explanation: After did, the main verb is in the base form: see.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses 'does'?
explanation: After does, the main verb remains in the base form.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses 'used to'?
option1: I used to walk to school.
option2: I use to walked to school.
option3: I used to walking to school.
option4: I use to walk to school yesterday.
explanation: Used to is followed by the base verb to describe a past habit.

questionText: Which word is a pronoun in the sentence 'They waited outside'?
explanation: They is a pronoun replacing a noun or noun phrase.

questionText: Choose the correct pronoun: 'Sam and ___ went to the library.'
explanation: I is the subject pronoun needed before went.

questionText: Choose the correct pronoun: 'The teacher spoke to Alex and ___.'
explanation: Me is the object pronoun after the preposition to.

questionText: Choose the correct possessive determiner: '___ book is on the desk.'
explanation: My is a possessive determiner used before a noun.

questionText: Choose the correct possessive pronoun: 'The blue bag is ___.'
explanation: Mine can stand alone as a possessive pronoun.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'they're' correctly?
option4: Their are going to the park.
explanation: They're is the contraction of they are.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'there' correctly?
explanation: There refers to a place.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'their' correctly?
explanation: Their is the possessive determiner before bags.

questionText: Choose the correct article: 'She adopted ___ unusual pet.'
explanation: An is used before a vowel sound, and unusual begins with a vowel sound.

questionText: Choose the correct article: 'He waited for ___ hour.'
explanation: Hour begins with a vowel sound, so an is used.

questionText: Choose the correct determiner: 'There aren't ___ apples left.'
explanation: Many is used with countable plural nouns such as apples.

questionText: Choose the correct determiner: 'There isn't ___ milk left.'
explanation: Much is used with uncountable nouns such as milk.

questionText: Which sentence correctly treats 'team' as a single unit?
option1: The team is winning every match.
option2: The team are winning every match.
option3: The team be winning every match.
explanation: When the team is explicitly treated as one unit, the singular verb is is appropriate.

questionText: Which sentence has correct agreement?
option1: Each of the pupils have a locker.
option2: Each of the pupils has a locker.
option3: Each of the pupils having a locker.
option4: Each of the pupils are a locker.
explanation: Each is singular and takes has.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'everyone' correctly?
explanation: Everyone is grammatically singular and takes has.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'fewer' correctly?
option1: There are fewer cars on the road today.
explanation: Fewer is normally used with countable plural nouns such as cars.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'less' correctly?
option1: There are less books on the shelf.
option2: There is less water in the bottle.
explanation: Less is used with uncountable nouns such as water.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'each' correctly?
explanation: Each is singular, so the singular verb has is required.

questionText: Which sentence uses a countable noun correctly?
option2: I need two pieces of advice.
explanation: Advice is uncountable; two pieces of advice is the standard form.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'information' correctly?
option2: She gave me three pieces of information.
explanation: Information is uncountable, so pieces of information is used for separate items.

questionText: Which sentence uses a collective noun correctly?
option1: The flock of birds flew south.
option2: The flock of birds flyed south.
option3: The flock of birds flying south.
option4: The flock of birds have flew south.
explanation: Flock is a collective noun and flew is the correct past form.

questionText: Which sentence uses a reflexive pronoun correctly?
explanation: Myself correctly refers back to the subject I.

questionText: Which sentence uses a demonstrative pronoun correctly?
explanation: These is the plural demonstrative pronoun used with shoes.

questionText: Which word is an adjective in 'The enormous elephant walked slowly'?
explanation: Enormous describes the noun elephant.

questionText: Which word is an adverb in 'The athlete ran quickly'?
explanation: Quickly describes how the athlete ran.

questionText: Choose the correct comparative form: 'This book is ___ than that one.'
explanation: More interesting is the comparative form.

questionText: Choose the correct superlative form: 'That was the ___ film I have seen.'
explanation: Most exciting is the superlative form.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'good' and 'well' correctly?
explanation: Well is the adverb used to describe how she sings.

questionText: Choose the correct preposition: 'The keys are ___ the table.'
explanation: On indicates the keys are positioned on the surface of the table.

questionText: Choose the correct preposition: 'We arrived ___ the station at six.'
explanation: At is commonly used with specific points or places such as a station.

questionText: Choose the correct preposition: 'She is interested ___ science.'
explanation: The standard phrase is interested in.

questionText: Choose the correct conjunction: 'I stayed indoors ___ it was raining.'
explanation: Because introduces the reason for staying indoors.

questionText: Choose the correct conjunction: 'I wanted to go, ___ I was too tired.'
explanation: But shows contrast between wanting to go and being too tired.

questionText: Choose the correct conjunction: 'You can have tea ___ coffee.'
explanation: Or presents alternatives.

questionText: Choose the correct conjunction: 'It was cold, ___ we wore coats.'
explanation: So introduces the result of it being cold.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'although' correctly?
option1: Although it was raining, we went outside.
option2: Although it was raining, but we went outside.
option3: Although it was raining so we went outside.
option4: Although because it was raining, we went outside.
explanation: Although introduces a contrast and does not need but in the same clause.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'unless' correctly?
option1: You will miss the bus unless you hurry.
option2: You will miss the bus unless you will hurry.
option3: You will miss the bus unless you hurried tomorrow.
option4: You will miss the bus unless to hurry.
explanation: Unless means if not and is followed by the present tense in this future condition.

questionText: Which sentence uses an adverbial phrase correctly?
option1: He completed the task with great care.
option2: He completed the task great careful.
option3: He completed the task careful great.
option4: He completed the task with care great.
explanation: With great care is an adverbial phrase explaining how the task was completed.

questionText: Which sentence contains a prepositional phrase?
option1: The cat slept under the table.
explanation: Under the table is a prepositional phrase.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'than' correctly?
option1: My sister is taller then me.
option2: My sister is taller than me.
option3: My sister is more tall then me.
option4: My sister is tallest than me.
explanation: Than is used when making a comparison.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'then' correctly?
option1: First finish your work, then you can play.
option2: First finish your work, than you can play.
option3: First finish your work, than you could play.
option4: First finish your work, then than you can play.
explanation: Then indicates what happens next in time.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'between' correctly?
option1: The choice is between tea and coffee.
option2: The choice is between tea or coffee.
option3: The choice is among tea and coffee.
option4: The choice is between tea to coffee.
explanation: Between is used for a relationship involving two choices here.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'among' correctly?
option1: She shared the sweets among the five children.
option2: She shared the sweets among the two children.
option3: She shared the sweets between the five children.
option4: She shared the sweets among to five children.
explanation: Among is commonly used when something is distributed within a group.

questionText: Which sentence is a compound sentence?
option1: Although it was raining, we played.
option2: The bell rang, and the pupils left.
option3: Running quickly, he caught the bus.
explanation: The second sentence joins two main clauses with and.

questionText: Which sentence is a complex sentence?
option2: The sun shone, and we went outside.
option3: Because the sun shone, we went outside.
explanation: Because the sun shone is a subordinate clause joined to a main clause.

questionText: Which sentence is interrogative?
option2: What time does the lesson start?
explanation: An interrogative sentence asks a question.

questionText: Which sentence is imperative?
explanation: An imperative gives a command or instruction.

questionText: Which sentence is exclamatory?
explanation: What a delicious cake! expresses strong feeling.

questionText: Which sentence is declarative?
explanation: A declarative sentence makes a statement.

questionText: Which reported speech sentence is correct?
option2: Tom said that I am tired.
option3: Tom said that he was tired.
option4: Tom said that he is tired yesterday.
explanation: In reported speech, I changes to he and am commonly shifts to was when reporting in the past.

questionText: Which direct speech sentence correctly reports: Sarah said that she was hungry?
explanation: The speaker Sarah would use I when speaking directly.

questionText: Which sentence uses a relative pronoun correctly?
option1: The boy which won the race smiled.
option2: The boy who won the race smiled.
option3: The boy where won the race smiled.
option4: The boy when won the race smiled.
explanation: Who is used for people.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'which' correctly?
option1: The car which I bought is blue.
option2: The car who I bought is blue.
option3: The car where I bought is blue.
option4: The car whom I bought is blue.
explanation: Which can refer to a thing such as a car.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'whose' correctly?
option1: The girl whose bag was lost is here.
option2: The girl who's bag was lost is here.
option3: The girl which bag was lost is here.
option4: The girl who bag was lost is here.
explanation: Whose shows possession in a relative clause.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'whom' correctly in formal English?
option1: Whom did you invite to the party?
option2: Whom is coming to the party?
explanation: Whom is used as the object of invite in formal English.

questionText: Which sentence contains a dangling modifier?
option1: Walking to school, I saw a rainbow.
option2: Walking to school, the rainbow appeared.
option3: I saw a rainbow while walking to school.
option4: While I walked to school, I saw a rainbow.
explanation: The opening phrase Walking to school incorrectly appears to modify the rainbow.

questionText: Which sentence avoids a misplaced modifier?
option1: She almost finished all the homework.
option2: She finished almost all the homework.
option3: She finished all almost the homework.
option4: Almost she finished all the homework.
explanation: Almost correctly modifies all in the phrase almost all the homework.

questionText: Which sentence uses parallel structure correctly?
option1: She likes reading, swimming and cycling.
option2: She likes reading, to swim and cycling.
option3: She likes to read, swimming and to cycle.
option4: She likes read, swimming and cycling.
explanation: The three activities use the same -ing form.

questionText: Which sentence uses a gerund correctly?
explanation: Swimming functions as a gerund, acting as the subject of the sentence.

questionText: Which sentence uses an infinitive correctly?
explanation: The infinitive is to learn.

questionText: Which sentence uses a conditional correctly?
option1: If I had time, I would help you.
option2: If I will have time, I would help you.
option3: If I had time, I will helped you.
option4: If I have had time, I would helped you.
explanation: This is a standard second conditional: if + past simple, would + base verb.

questionText: Which sentence uses the first conditional correctly?
option1: If it rains, we will stay inside.
option2: If it will rain, we stay inside.
option3: If it rained, we will stay inside.
option4: If it rains, we would stayed inside.
explanation: The first conditional uses present simple in the if-clause and will + base verb in the main clause.

questionText: Which sentence uses 'each' with the correct verb?
option1: Each of the two players has a locker.
option2: Each of the two players have a locker.
option3: Each of the two players having a locker.
option4: Each of the two players are a locker.
explanation: Each is singular, so it takes has.
